trigger: P0575-P0575B showed that the replicated arrival density worsens raw source-plane consistency under the ordinary Poisson relation in every family split.
question: Can the same baryonic destination field predict held-out raw image positions if only its conversion into deflection has a different scale response?

formula.interpretation: p>1 emphasizes long-wavelength routed deflection; p<1 emphasizes short-wavelength routed deflection. This breaks the ordinary single-Poisson link between apparent density and deflection and is explicitly a new-physics diagnostic.

selection.rule: Select one p and f_alpha by minimum source-plane RMS on calibration families only, fitting one positive overall amplitude per candidate; score the locked candidate on held-out families without refit.

cross_domain.Solar: Q90=0 and C=1, so the routed component is absent and the standard local field remains.
cross_domain.SPARC: Deprojected axisymmetric profiles have Q90=0, so the fractional routed propagator changes all 175 rotation curves by exactly zero.
cross_domain.cluster_map: The P0574 destination morphology and its 60 kpc spatial extent are held fixed; only the deflection propagator changes.

claim_limits: A successful fractional power would be phenomenology, not a covariant field equation or derivation from an action.
The same one cluster and 12 positions are reused; only the family split is prospective to this propagator grid.
One normalized-map amplitude is still fitted and absolute gravity strength is not predicted.
The baryon proxy omits gas, intracluster light, and stellar mass-to-light variation.
The source-plane statistic is not full image-plane root finding.
